learn.hook: One samosa costs ₹15, two cost ₹30, ten cost ₹150. Double the samosas and you double the bill. That is direct proportion!
points: Two quantities are in direct proportion if, when one is multiplied by a number, the other is multiplied by the same number.
In direct proportion, y ÷ x stays the same. We can write y = kx, where k is the constant.
Examples: number of pens and their cost; petrol used and distance at a steady speed; time and pay for a fixed hourly wage.
Test a table: divide each y by its x. If you always get the same number, it is direct proportion.
Not everything that grows together is in proportion. A child's age and height both grow, but height does not double when age doubles.

example.q: 5 m of cloth costs ₹350. What is the cost of 8 m?
steps: Cost ÷ length stays the same: 350 ÷ 5 = ₹70 per metre

learn.reallife: Your phone data bill, petrol pump meters and auto-rickshaw fares (after the minimum charge) grow in direct proportion.

games.title: Direct or not?
items: Number of pens and their total cost
Distance travelled at a steady speed and time taken
Litres of petrol and its cost
Laddoos made and kg of sugar used (same recipe)
A child's age and height
Number of workers and days to finish a job
Speed and time for a fixed journey
A person's age and weight

items.text: If 3 pens cost ₹36, then 6 pens cost ₹___
x and y in direct proportion: x = 2, y = 14; x = 5, y = ___
If y = 4x, then when x = 9, y = ___
In direct proportion, y ÷ x stays ___

quiz.q: 5 m of cloth costs ₹350. What is the cost of 8 m?
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 to the price because 8 is 3 more than 5

quiz.q: x and y are in direct proportion. When x = 6, y = 15. What is y when x = 10?
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 to y because x went up by 4

quiz.q: Which pair of quantities is in direct proportion?
options: Number of workers and time to build a wall
Number of tickets bought and total cost
Age and height of a child
Speed of a car and time for a fixed trip
quiz.explain: Each ticket costs the same, so twice the tickets cost twice as much. The others are not direct proportion.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any two quantities that change together are directly proportional

quiz.q: A car uses 6 litres of petrol to travel 90 km. How far can it go on 10 litres?
quiz.explain: It goes 90 ÷ 6 = 15 km per litre, so on 10 litres it goes 150 km.
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 km for the 4 extra litres

quiz.q: x and y are in direct proportion. When x is 3, 5 and 8, y is 12, 20 and ?. What is the missing y?
quiz.mistake: Adds 8 to 20 instead of using the constant ratio

quiz.q: Meena types 270 words in 6 minutes at a steady speed. How many words does she type in 15 minutes?
quiz.explain: She types 270 ÷ 6 = 45 words a minute. In 15 minutes: 45 × 15 = 675 words.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies 270 by 6 instead of dividing

quiz.q: A photocopier makes 80 copies in 4 minutes. How many minutes does it take to make 300 copies?
quiz.explain: It makes 80 ÷ 4 = 20 copies a minute. 300 ÷ 20 = 15 minutes.
quiz.mistake: Divides 300 by 4 instead of by the copies per minute

quiz.q: Joseph says: 'In direct proportion, when x doubles, y goes up by 2.' What is the correct statement?
options: When x doubles, y also doubles
When x doubles, y is halved
When x doubles, y goes up by 2
When x doubles, y stays the same
quiz.explain: In direct proportion y = kx. If x is multiplied by 2, y is multiplied by 2 as well.
quiz.mistake: Confuses multiplying by 2 with adding 2

teach.ask: Gappu asks: How can I tell if the cost of bananas is in direct proportion to the number of bananas?
teach.praise: Divide cost by number for each pair. If it is always the same, it is direct proportion. Banana-tastic!
teach.nudge: If you buy twice as many bananas, what happens to the cost? What stays the same?

learn.hook: On a map of India, Delhi and Jaipur are about 4 cm apart. With the right scale, that tiny gap becomes about 240 km!
points: Check a proportion a : b :: c : d by cross-multiplying: it holds exactly when a × d = b × c.
A map scale like 1 : 60,00,000 is a ratio: 1 cm on the map stands for 60,00,000 cm = 60 km on the ground.
Map to real: multiply by the scale. Real to map: change to the same unit, then divide. At 1 : 50,000, a real 4 km = 4,00,000 cm becomes 8 cm on the map.
A map gives the straight-line (geographical) distance. The road distance is usually longer, because roads bend around hills, rivers and towns.
Make your own map: measure your classroom and draw it to scale, for example 1 : 100 (1 cm for 1 m).

example.q: On a map with scale 1 : 60,00,000, two cities are 4 cm apart. How far apart are they really?

learn.reallife: Google Maps, school atlases and house plans all depend on scales.

items.q: 1 : 50,000 — 4 km is how many cm on the map?
1 : 100 — a 9 m wall is how many cm?

games.title: Maps and proportions
items: 4 : 10 :: 6 : 15 is a true proportion.
The road distance between two towns is never longer than the map's straight-line distance.
Roads bend, so road distance is usually longer.
A scale of 1 : 100 means 1 cm on the drawing is 1 m in real life.
3 : 5 :: 9 : 16 is a true proportion.

quiz.q: Are 4 : 10 and 6 : 15 in proportion?
quiz.explain: Cross-multiply: 4 × 15 = 60 and 10 × 6 = 60. They are equal, so the ratios are in proportion.
quiz.mistake: Multiplies the wrong pairs or compares differences

quiz.q: A map has scale 1 : 60,00,000. Two towns are 5 cm apart on it. What is the straight-line distance between them?
quiz.mistake: Gets the units wrong when changing cm into km

quiz.q: At a scale of 1 : 50,000, how long is a real distance of 4 km on the map?
quiz.mistake: Divides without first changing km into cm

quiz.q: A map says '1 cm = 25 km'. How is this written as a ratio scale?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to change km into cm

quiz.q: The map distance between two villages gives 30 km, but the bus travels 42 km. Why?
options: Buses always travel twice the distance
The road bends, so it is longer than the straight-line distance
quiz.explain: A map's scale distance is a straight line; real roads curve around obstacles.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the map shows road length

quiz.q: A classroom is 8 m long. It is drawn at a scale of 1 : 100. How long is it on the drawing?
quiz.mistake: Divides 8 m by 100 without changing units

quiz.q: A 9 m wall is drawn at a scale of 1 : 50. How long is it on the drawing?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 50 instead of dividing

quiz.q: Are 3, 7, 12, 28 in proportion (3 : 7 :: 12 : 28)?
options: Yes, because all are whole numbers
quiz.mistake: Compares differences instead of products

teach.ask: Gappu found Pune and Mumbai 2 cm apart on a map with scale 1 : 60,00,000. How far should he fly in a straight line?
teach.praise: 2.5 × 60 = 150 km in a straight line. Flying birds don't need roads!
teach.nudge: How many km does 1 cm stand for on this map?

topics.title: Ratios with more than two terms

learn.hook: Garam masala, concrete and tie-dye paint all follow three-part (or more!) ratios. Change one part and you must change them all.
points: A ratio can have many terms, like cumin : coriander : chilli = 2 : 3 : 1. To scale it, multiply EVERY term by the same number: 4 : 6 : 2.
Mixtures: concrete is often cement : sand : gravel = 1 : 2 : 4; paints and spice mixes use ratios too.
To divide a quantity in a : b : c, add the terms, find one part, then multiply. ₹1800 in 2 : 3 : 4 → 9 parts, 1 part = ₹200 → ₹400, ₹600, ₹800.
The same method shares time, books or coins: 120 minutes in 3 : 2 : 1 gives 60, 40 and 20 minutes.

example.q: A 300 g spice mix has cumin : coriander : chilli = 2 : 3 : 1. How much coriander is in it?

learn.reallife: Masons mix cement, sand and gravel by ratio — a wrong mix makes weak walls!

quiz.q: A 300 g spice mix has cumin : coriander : chilli = 2 : 3 : 1. How many grams of coriander does it contain?
quiz.explain: 6 parts in all; 1 part = 50 g; coriander = 3 parts = 150 g.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 3 terms instead of 6 parts

quiz.q: The same 2 : 3 : 1 spice mix is made with 6 teaspoons of chilli. How many teaspoons of cumin are needed?
quiz.mistake: Adds 5 to every term

quiz.q: Concrete uses cement : sand : gravel = 1 : 2 : 4. How many bags of gravel go into a 35-bag mix?
quiz.explain: 7 parts in all; 1 part = 5 bags; gravel = 4 × 5 = 20 bags.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 3 instead of the total parts

quiz.q: Paint is mixed red : white : yellow = 1 : 3 : 2. If 9 L of white is used, what is the total amount of paint?
quiz.explain: White 3 → 9 is × 3, so the mix is 3 : 9 : 6, a total of 18 L.
quiz.mistake: Adds only two of the parts

quiz.q: ₹1800 is divided in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. What is the largest share?
quiz.mistake: Divides into 3 equal shares

quiz.q: Diya splits 120 minutes of study between maths, science and English in the ratio 3 : 2 : 1. How long is maths?
quiz.mistake: Uses 3 out of 3 + 2 instead of all 6 parts

quiz.q: 60 books are shared among three classes in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3. How many does the middle class get?
quiz.explain: 6 parts; 1 part = 10 books; the middle share is 2 × 10 = 20.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 3

quiz.q: A purse has ₹1, ₹2 and ₹5 coins in the ratio 5 : 3 : 1 by number. The total is ₹48. How many ₹2 coins are there?
quiz.explain: One 'set' of 5, 3 and 1 coins is worth 5 + 6 + 5 = ₹16. ₹48 is 3 sets, so there are 3 × 3 = 9 ₹2 coins.
quiz.mistake: Splits the money in 5 : 3 : 1 instead of the coin counts

teach.ask: Gappu's grandma makes chai masala with ginger : cardamom : pepper = 3 : 2 : 1. He wants 60 g. How much of each?
teach.praise: 6 parts, 10 g each: 30 g ginger, 20 g cardamom and 10 g pepper. Grandma's chai, Gappu-sized!
teach.nudge: How many parts are there altogether? How much is one part?

learn.hook: Can a triangle have sides in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3? Try building it with straws — it just falls flat!
points: Angles of a triangle add to 180°. If they are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4, the 9 parts make 180°, so 1 part = 20° and the angles are 40°, 60°, 80°.
A ratio like 1 : 2 : 3 for angles gives 30°, 60°, 90° — a right triangle.
Sides in a ratio: 2 : 3 : 4 with perimeter 36 cm gives 1 part = 4 cm, so sides 8, 12 and 16 cm.
Triangle inequality: the two shorter sides must add up to MORE than the longest. 1 : 2 : 3 fails (1 + 2 = 3), so no triangle can be made. 4 : 5 : 6 works.

example.q: A triangle's angles are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. Find them.

learn.reallife: Roof trusses and bridge supports are designed with side ratios that are sure to make strong triangles.

games.title: Can these be the sides of a triangle?

quiz.q: A triangle's angles are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4. What is the largest angle?
quiz.explain: 9 parts = 180°, so 1 part = 20° and the largest is 4 × 20° = 80°.
quiz.mistake: Uses 360° instead of 180°

quiz.q: A triangle's angles are in the ratio 1 : 1 : 2. What is its largest angle?
quiz.explain: 4 parts = 180°, so 1 part = 45° and the angles are 45°, 45°, 90°.
quiz.mistake: Divides 180 by 3 because there are 3 angles

quiz.q: A triangle's angles are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3. What is the smallest angle?
quiz.mistake: Divides by 3 instead of 6

quiz.q: A triangle's sides are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4 and its perimeter is 36 cm. How long is the longest side?
quiz.explain: 9 parts = 36 cm, so 1 part = 4 cm and the longest side is 4 × 4 = 16 cm.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 3 sides instead of 9 parts

quiz.q: Can a triangle have sides in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3?
options: No — the two shorter sides only equal the longest, so they lie flat
Yes — it makes a right triangle
No — the sides must all be equal
quiz.explain: For sides k, 2k, 3k: k + 2k = 3k. The shorter sides must add to MORE than the longest, so no triangle forms.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the triangle inequality

quiz.q: A triangle has sides in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5 and perimeter 24 cm. What are its sides?
quiz.explain: 12 parts = 24 cm, so 1 part = 2 cm: sides 6, 8, 10 cm (a right triangle, since 6² + 8² = 10²).
quiz.mistake: Uses the ratio numbers as lengths

quiz.q: Which ratio can be the sides of a triangle?
quiz.explain: 4 + 5 = 9 > 6, so a triangle forms. In the others the two smaller numbers add to less than the largest.
quiz.mistake: Checks only that the numbers are different

quiz.q: A triangle's angles are in the ratio 5 : 6 : 7. What is the middle-sized angle?
quiz.explain: 18 parts = 180°, so 1 part = 10° and the middle angle is 6 × 10° = 60°.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 3

teach.ask: Gappu has three twigs in the ratio 1 : 1 : 3. He wants a triangle-shaped perch. Will it work?
teach.praise: No! 1 + 1 is less than 3, so the twigs can't meet. I need the two short ones to be longer together than the long one.
teach.nudge: What must be true about the two shorter sides compared with the longest side?

topics.title: A slice of the pie: pie charts

learn.hook: A pie chart is a rotī cut fairly: each slice's angle shows its share of the whole 360°.
points: A pie chart shows parts of a whole as sectors (slices) of a circle.
Each sector's central angle is proportional to its value: angle = (value ÷ total) × 360°. All angles add to 360°.
From percentages: angle = percentage × 3.6°. So 25% gives 90° and 40% gives 144°.
To draw it: find each angle, draw a radius, measure the first angle with a protractor from it, then measure the next angle from the new line, and so on. Label each sector.
To read it: value = (angle ÷ 360°) × total. A 72° sector of 500 students is 72/360 × 500 = 100 students.

example.q: In a survey of 36 students, 12 like cricket, 9 like football and 15 like kabaddi. Find the sector angles.

learn.reallife: Budget news on TV often shows where each rupee goes using a pie chart.

games.title: Draw a pie chart
items: Find the total
Work out each angle: value ÷ total × 360°
Draw a circle and one radius
Measure each angle with a protractor, one after another
Label each sector

quiz.q: 30 out of 120 students walk to school. What is the angle of the 'walk' sector in a pie chart?
quiz.mistake: Uses the count itself as the angle

quiz.q: In a pie chart, a category makes up 40% of the total. What is its sector angle?
quiz.mistake: Uses the percentage as the angle

quiz.q: A pie chart shows 500 students. The 'music club' sector is 72°. How many students are in the music club?
quiz.mistake: Reads the angle as the number of students

quiz.q: A sector of a pie chart has an angle of 60°. What fraction of the whole does it show?
quiz.mistake: Divides by 100 instead of 360

quiz.q: In a survey of 36 students, 12 like cricket. What is the angle of the cricket sector?
quiz.mistake: Uses 100 as the whole instead of 360°

quiz.q: A family's budget of ₹30,000 is shown in a pie chart. The rent sector is 108°. How much is the rent?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies the angle by 100

quiz.q: What do all the sector angles of a pie chart add up to?
quiz.explain: The sectors fill the whole circle, which is 360°.
quiz.mistake: Confuses angles with percentages

quiz.q: When drawing a pie chart with a protractor, where do you measure the second sector's angle from?
options: From the same starting radius again
From the line that ends the first sector
From the top of the page
From the centre outwards in any direction
quiz.explain: Sectors are placed side by side, so each new angle starts where the last one ended.
quiz.mistake: Measures every sector from the same starting line, so they overlap

teach.ask: Gappu asked 20 birds their favourite food: 10 said seeds, 5 worms, 5 berries. How should he draw the pie chart?
teach.praise: Seeds get 180° (half), worms 90°, berries 90°. My bird-food pie chart is ready!
teach.nudge: What fraction of the birds chose seeds? What angle is that?

learn.hook: One painter takes 12 days to paint a house. Do 3 painters also take 12 days? No, just 4 days! More hands, fewer days.
points: Two quantities are in inverse proportion if, when one is multiplied by a number, the other is divided by the same number.
In inverse proportion, x × y stays the same.
Examples: workers and days for a fixed job; speed and time for a fixed distance; number of children and laddoos each gets from a fixed box.
To solve: find the fixed product first, then divide by the new value.
Not every 'one goes up, other goes down' is inverse proportion. Check that the product stays the same.

example.q: 6 workers build a wall in 10 days. How long will 15 workers take at the same rate?

learn.reallife: More checkout counters at a shop mean shorter queues, and a faster train means a shorter journey time.

items.q: 6 workers take 10 days. 12 workers take how many days?
4 taps fill a tank in 6 hours. 8 taps take how many hours?
At 50 km/h a trip takes 4 hours. At 100 km/h, how many hours?
15 children get 8 laddoos each. With 20 children, how many each?
3 pumps empty a tank in 12 hours. 9 pumps take how many hours?

quiz.q: 6 workers build a wall in 10 days. How many days will 15 workers take, working at the same rate?
quiz.mistake: Treats it as direct proportion and gets 25 days

quiz.q: A train at 60 km/h takes 5 hours for a journey. How many hours does it take at 75 km/h?
quiz.mistake: Uses direct proportion and gets a longer time

quiz.q: Which pair of quantities is in inverse proportion?
options: Distance and time at a steady speed
Litres of milk and its cost
Speed and time for a fixed distance
quiz.explain: For a fixed distance, speed × time = distance stays the same. Double the speed, half the time.
quiz.mistake: Picks a direct proportion pair

quiz.q: x and y are in inverse proportion. When x = 8, y = 9. What is y when x = 12?
quiz.mistake: Uses direct proportion (gets 13.5)

quiz.q: A camp has enough food for 40 children for 15 days. If 10 more children join, how many days will the food last?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the new children, or uses direct proportion

quiz.q: Riya shares a box of laddoos equally. With 8 friends, each gets 9 laddoos. How many does each get if there are 12 friends?
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 more laddoos because there are 4 more friends

quiz.q: Which table shows x and y in inverse proportion?
quiz.explain: 2 × 12 = 4 × 6 = 8 × 3 = 24. The product stays the same, so it is inverse proportion.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any decreasing table is inverse proportion without checking products

quiz.q: 4 pipes fill a tank in 3 hours. How many such pipes are needed to fill it in 1 hour?
quiz.mistake: Thinks fewer hours means fewer pipes

teach.ask: Gappu asks: 2 birds eat a pile of seeds in 6 hours. How long will 4 birds take?
teach.praise: 2 × 6 = 12 bird-hours stays the same, so 4 birds take 12 ÷ 4 = 3 hours. More birds, less time!
teach.nudge: When the number of birds doubles, what happens to the time? What stays the same?

learn.hook: Ravi paints a wall in 6 days and Sita in 3 days. Working together, do they take 9 days? 4.5? Neither — they finish in 2!
points: Think of the rate: if Ravi takes 6 days for the whole job, he does 1/6 of it each day. Sita does 1/3 each day.
Working together, the rates add: 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2 of the job per day, so together they take 2 days.
Pipes work the same way: one fills a tank in 4 hours, another in 6 hours. Together: 1/4 + 1/6 = 5/12 per hour, so 12/5 = 2.4 hours (2 hours 24 minutes).
A drain pipe works against you, so subtract its rate: fill in 3 hours, empty in 6 hours → 1/3 − 1/6 = 1/6 per hour, so 6 hours to fill.

example.q: Ravi paints a wall in 6 days and Sita in 3 days. How long do they take together?

learn.reallife: Construction teams, kitchen staff and even two pumps in a housing society all 'work together' this way.

games.title: Together or not?
items: Two people working together always take the average of their times.
Rates add; the time is shorter than either person alone.
If A does 1/8 of a job per day, A alone takes 8 days.
8 × 1/8 = 1 whole job.
A drain pipe's rate is subtracted from a filling pipe's rate.
It removes water while the other adds.
Two equal workers who each take 10 days finish together in 5 days.

quiz.q: Ravi paints a wall in 6 days and Sita paints it in 3 days. How many days do they take together?
quiz.explain: Rates: 1/6 + 1/3 = 1/2 of the wall per day, so 2 days.
quiz.mistake: Adds or averages the times

quiz.q: One pipe fills a tank in 4 hours and another in 6 hours. How long do both together take?
quiz.explain: 1/4 + 1/6 = 5/12 per hour, so 12/5 = 2.4 hours (2 h 24 min).
quiz.mistake: Averages the two times

quiz.q: A can finish a job in 10 days and B in 15 days. How many days do they take together?
quiz.mistake: Adds the days

quiz.q: A tap fills a tank in 3 hours, but a leak empties a full tank in 6 hours. With both open, how long does it take to fill?
quiz.explain: Fill rate 1/3 minus leak rate 1/6 = 1/6 per hour, so 6 hours.
quiz.mistake: Adds the leak rate instead of subtracting

quiz.q: Asha can do a job alone in 8 days. What fraction of the job does she do in one day?
quiz.explain: The whole job takes 8 days, so each day she does 1/8 of it.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number of days instead of the rate

quiz.q: Three taps fill a tank in 6, 12 and 4 hours. How long do all three take together?
quiz.mistake: Adds the times

quiz.q: Amit can finish a job in 12 days. He works 4 days and leaves; Bina finishes the rest in 6 days. How long would Bina take alone?
quiz.explain: Amit does 4/12 = 1/3. Bina does the remaining 2/3 in 6 days, so the whole job takes her 6 × 3/2 = 9 days.
quiz.mistake: Thinks Bina did the whole job in 6 days

quiz.q: Two workers who each take 10 days for a job work together. How many days do they take?
quiz.explain: 1/10 + 1/10 = 1/5 per day, so 5 days. This also fits inverse proportion: twice the workers, half the time.
quiz.mistake: Adds the days

teach.ask: Gappu builds a nest in 4 days and his friend Pari in 4 days too. Gappu thinks together they need 8 days. Help him!
teach.praise: Each of us does 1/4 a day, so together 1/2 a day — just 2 days! Teamwork is faster.
teach.nudge: How much of the nest does each bird build in one day?

learn.hook: The Vande Bharat Express can run at 160 km/h. A cheetah can sprint at over 100 km/h, but only for a few seconds. Who wins a long race? Rates tell the story!
points: A rate compares two different kinds of quantities: km per hour, ₹ per kg, words per minute, heartbeats per minute.
A unit rate is the amount for 1 unit: 300 km in 5 hours is 60 km per hour.
Speed = distance ÷ time, distance = speed × time, time = distance ÷ speed.
To change km/h to m/s, multiply by 1000/3600 = 5/18. So 72 km/h = 20 m/s.
Average speed = total distance ÷ total time. It is not always the average of the two speeds.

example.q: A train goes 180 km in 2 hours and then 120 km in 2 hours. What is its average speed?

learn.reallife: Cricket commentators give run rates per over, doctors check pulse rate per minute, and shops show price per kg.

games.title: Slowest to fastest
items: Walking at 5 km/h
Cycling 3 km in 12 minutes
Auto-rickshaw: 50 km in 2 hours
Car at 20 m/s
Train: 450 km in 5 hours

games.title: Rate check
items: 36 km/h is the same as 10 m/s.
Going 60 km/h for 1 hour and then 40 km/h for 1 hour gives an average speed of 50 km/h.
Total 100 km in 2 hours = 50 km/h. The times are equal, so here it works.
Going 60 km at 60 km/h and then 60 km at 40 km/h gives an average speed of 50 km/h.
Time = 1 h + 1.5 h = 2.5 h, so average = 120 ÷ 2.5 = 48 km/h.
At ₹40 per kg, 3 kg cost ₹120.
Speed = time ÷ distance.
Speed = distance ÷ time.
A heart rate is measured in beats per minute.
It counts heartbeats in each minute.

quiz.q: A bus travels 240 km in 4 hours. What is its speed in km per hour?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies distance by time

quiz.q: Change 72 km/h into metres per second. What is the number of m/s?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies by 3.6 instead of dividing (gets 259.2)

quiz.q: Kabir cycles at 15 km/h. How long does he take to cover 45 km?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies distance by speed, or divides speed by distance

quiz.q: Aisha walks 2 km to school in 30 minutes. What is her speed in km/h?
quiz.mistake: Divides minutes by km (30 ÷ 2 = 15) without changing to hours

quiz.q: A train travels 180 km in 2 hours and then 120 km in 2 hours. What is its average speed for the whole trip in km/h?
quiz.explain: Total distance 300 km in total time 4 hours: 300 ÷ 4 = 75 km/h.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 2 hours only, or gives total distance

quiz.q: Rice costs ₹480 for 8 kg. What is the rate per kg?
quiz.mistake: Multiplies instead of dividing

quiz.q: A heart beats 72 times a minute. How many times does it beat in one hour?
quiz.mistake: Adds 60 instead of multiplying, or multiplies by 10

quiz.q: Joseph drives 60 km at 60 km/h and then another 60 km at 30 km/h. What is his average speed for the whole trip in km/h?
quiz.explain: Time: 60 ÷ 60 = 1 h and 60 ÷ 30 = 2 h. Total 120 km in 3 hours = 40 km/h.
quiz.mistake: Averages the two speeds (45) even though the times are different

teach.ask: Gappu asks: I flew 30 km in 2 hours. How do I find my speed?
teach.praise: Distance divided by time: 30 ÷ 2 = 15 km per hour. Zoom zoom, Gappu!
teach.nudge: Which two numbers do you need, and do you multiply or divide them?
